"Elster Metering Ltd" vs "Elster Water Metering Limited"

This is a tricky one. "Elster Metering" vs "Elster Water Metering" — is "Water" a meaningful difference? Elster Water Metering Limited is a real UK company (formerly Elster Metering Limited / part of Elster Group, later Honeywell). Actually, in the UK, there was "Elster Metering Limited" which was renamed to "Elster Water Metering Limited" around 2012-2013 when the electricity metering business (Elster Electricity) was sold. The company "Elster Metering Ltd" changed its name to "Elster Water Metering Limited" in 2013 (I believe around June 2013), since the water metering business stayed with Honeywell after Elster Electricity was divested to Melrose.

The certificate issuing year is 2013, and the document says "Elster Water Metering Limited". The register says "Elster Metering Ltd". These could refer to the same legal entity at different points in time — a name change. So this is a genuine different surface text but likely the same legal entity (name change).

But per the rules given:
- spelling drift, legal-suffix drift, accent differences = same-entity
- "Elster Metering Ltd" → "Elster Water Metering Limited": the suffix drift (Ltd → Limited) is same-entity, but the insertion of "Water" is more than spelling drift. It's a substantive name difference.

The rules say: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."
